pages.text: Calculus is the art of the infinitely small. $(item)Infinitesimals$() come from the reals. With a $(item)Function Graph$() they become $(item)Derivative$() and $(item)Integral Operators$() - rates of change and sums of slices.
Together those make $(item)Differential Manifolds$() - curved spaces smooth enough to do calculus on. They are the stage relativity is written on.

Complex analysis gives $(item)Fourier Series$() (any wave as a sum of pure tones) and $(item)Fractal Sets$().$(br2)Number theory needs $(item)Prime Shards$() - mined in the Platonic Realm, or sieved slowly from naturals - for $(item)Modular Forms$() and the $(item)Riemann Zeta Crystal$(). Riemann's zeros still guard the primes.
Smaller than every positive number, yet not zero.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
A rule that sends every input to exactly one output - drawn as a curve of light.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
The area under a curve, summed from infinitely many infinitesimal slices.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
A space that is flat up close and curved far away - the stage on which relativity is written.$(br2)Made in $(item)Topology Kiln$().
Any signal is a sum of waves. This one is a sum of all of them.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
z → z² + c, iterated forever. Infinitely detailed at every scale.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
